public_body: Webster Fire Department Board Of Engineers
overall: The AG found the Fire Department Board of Engineers did not violate the Open Meeting Law: it met in open session throughout, and a topic arising within 48 hours of a meeting need not appear in the notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to timely post that it would meet in executive session at its July 2010 meeting, which was held in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not giving the complainant notice that it intended to discuss this matter in open session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the impromptu executive session deprived him of due process of law.
allegations.key_passage: While a public body may choose to discuss complaints or charges brought against a public officer behind closed doors, there is no requirement that such a discussion occur in executive session, and the subject of the discussion has no right under the Open Meeting Law to demand that they do so.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to list discussion of him as a topic in the notice for its July 26, 2010 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the incident occurred within 48 hours of the meeting, the Board did not need to include the topic in the meeting notice.
